svg.title: Neutron-induced fission
svg.desc: (a) A neutron strikes a large nucleus and is absorbed. (b) The nucleus deforms like a struck liquid drop and narrows in the middle. (c) With fewer nucleons in contact, the Coulomb repulsion between the positively charged halves pushes them apart. (d) The nucleus splits into two fission fragments, FF1 and FF2, and some neutrons fly away. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Neutron absorption can lead to fission and additional neutrons
A schematic sequence, not a calculated nuclear shape or fragment trajectory. This channel conserves A
and Z; fragment kinetic energy, photons and later beta decays are omitted.
